links.outcome: Recall of Cochrane included studies by simulated user role (patient, clinician, researcher)
links.effect: Recall was lowest for the patient role (36.1% ± 29.3%) vs clinician (38.6% ± 28.9%) and researcher (42.8% ± 30.8%), p=2.0e-5; differences were small relative to variability.
links.quote: The researcher role yielded higher recall than the clinician or patient roles (42.8% $\pm$ 30.8% vs. 38.6% $\pm$ 28.9% vs. 36.1% $\pm$ 29.3%; $p=2.0\times10^{-5}$).

unlisted_practices: Benchmarking LLM chatbot study retrieval and citation quality against Cochrane systematic review included and excluded study sets
Assessing selection bias toward larger-sample-size trials in LLM-cited evidence

screen.reason: Evaluates the retrieval accuracy and citation quality of multiple commercial LLMs prompted with clinical questions benchmarked against Cochrane reviews, varying user role prompts.
